body:
Add an admin-only readiness endpoint on the EDP data-plane service that proves the shared backlog authority is reachable and reports the current global ID allocation state. This is a PF-SB pilot item; it does not change PF-GP agent workflows.

The endpoint is a real runtime path: edpsvc HTTP entrypoint -> edpdata.BacklogStore -> PostgreSQL global allocation + backlog_items. It must fail closed when the DB authority is unavailable and must never use local/Git ID fallback.
_note: Superseded by BI-PF-1509: 1508 has 5 design reviews vs budget 1, no material diff approval, and no coverage/standards under the new contract.

brief.why: Makes the shared DB authority observable before workers depend on it.
brief.problem: Operators and workers cannot inspect the authoritative DB backlog/ID state through the EDP service.
brief.what_adds: Admin-only GET /backlog/authority readiness endpoint with DB allocation/item counts.
brief.who_feels: PF-SB/PF-GP operators and workers diagnosing backlog authority failures.

decisions: Use /admin/backlog/authority to avoid the /backlog/{id} catch-all; buildMux is the sole /admin route owner and has no route registry
Use BacklogStore over the existing pgx pool, not a new store
Store reservation_count in backlog_id_allocations and maintain it with DB triggers on reservation insert/delete
Do not increment the counter in Reserve; idempotent retries return the existing block without touching the counter
Missing allocation row and missing migration/table both map to 503, never a zeroed 200
Auth runs before method checks: no bearer -> 401; valid bearer + POST -> 405
Production startup check fails closed; dev logs/metrics non-fatally
Scope item_count to the requested tenant because pf_app is RLS-enforced
Return no storage field; labels reservation_scope/item_scope make the response unambiguous
Endpoint is admin/human diagnostics only; internal callers use the control plane

A readiness endpoint must state tenant scope, migration dependencies, and alert routing explicitly

A missing global allocation row returns ErrAuthorityUnavailable -> 503, never a zeroed 200
backlog_items access is tenant-scoped by app.tenant_id and forced RLS
The runtime role is pf_app inheriting pf_runtime: NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS
No local JSON/Git fallback in DB mode
No DB DSN, token, item content, or cross-tenant item counts in the response
performance: allocation + reservation counter is a single PK row read; no count scan over reservations
item_count is tenant-scoped; existing idx_backlog_items_tenant_status supports the tenant filter; DBTimeout=5s maps to 503
endpoint is admin-only, not on worker hot path
dependencies: Prometheus/Alertmanager route in ops rule + runbook
requirements: GET /admin/backlog/authority?tenant=<tenant> without a bearer returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; status precedence is auth-first, so POST without a bearer is 401 and POST with a bearer is 405.

With a valid PF_ADMIN_TOKEN and tenant, GET /admin/backlog/authority returns 200 with authority=global, next_id from backlog_id_allocations, reservation_scope=global, reservation_count from the DB-maintained counter, tenant, item_scope=tenant, and item_count scoped to that tenant via forced RLS.
A missing tenant query parameter returns 400 and the handler never queries backlog_items without a tenant.
Missing migration 0016/0018, a missing global allocation row, DB outage, or query timeout returns 503 with a fixed backlog-authority-unavailable message; never a zeroed 200 or local/Git fallback.

An E2E test through edpsvc's real mux fails before the route is added and passes after it is wired; the scope guard rejects any new modified path outside the declared affected_files; no PF-GP agent/pipeline or backlog data files are changed.
observability: startup check: production fails closed; dev logs and sets edp_backlog_authority_startup_ok=0
handler increments edp_backlog_authority_errors_total on 503 and logs a redacted cause
runbook routes to platform on-call and documents /ready decoupling
existing limits request metrics record path/status

Counter changes on idempotent retry or out-of-band delete

api_contract: GET /admin/backlog/authority?tenant=<tenant>; adminOnly bearer; 401 before 405; 400 missing tenant; 200 authority snapshot; 503 fail-closed.

out_of_scope: No global cross-tenant item count (pf_app is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS)
No new DB role, SECURITY DEFINER function, or second ID authority
No move of the Python backlog domain or routes
No PF-GP agent/pipeline changes and no backlog item/file writes
verification: go test ./... in go/edpsvc with PF_RUNTIME_DSN
go test ./... in go/edpdata with PF_RUNTIME_DSN
language_rule: Shipped endpoint/store/migration is Go+SQL; scope guard is test tooling; alert rule/runbook are ops/docs; no new shipped Python product logic.

NIT: Response is assembled from two reads (allocation row vs tenant item_count) without a single snapshot; fine for diagnostics but note the possible skew in the runbook.
`to_regclass` validates tables, not the `reservation_count` column added by 0018; the missing-0018 case relies on a column error mapping to 503 — worth asserting the mapping in a test name/comment.
MAJOR: Fail-closed production startup means the process never runs when the DB is down, so `edp_backlog_authority_startup_ok` is never exported and the Prometheus rule `startup_ok == 0` is a dead branch; the alert cannot provide lead-time exactly when the failure occurs.

Counter invariant has a TRUNCATE hole: row-level INSERT/DELETE triggers do not fire on `TRUNCATE backlog_id_reservations`, so an out-of-band truncate silently zeroes the semantic count while the endpoint still returns 200 with a stale `reservation_count` (no drift-detection query or alert exists).

Fail-closed startup + single shared instance (CL-005) + shared DB makes DB blips/restarts a hard availability dependency with no stated bounded retry/backoff or recovery path before the orchestrator can bring the service up.
MINOR: Rollback ordering is ambiguous: "Remove route/startup check; migration 0018 down drops triggers/function/column" — down migration executed while the route is still live yields 503s; state the required order explicitly.
The scope-guard baseline `engineering/trails/BI-PF-1508-scope-baseline.txt` is referenced in test_matrix but not declared in `affected_files`; creating it may itself trip the guard.

Startup-check scope is unspecified (tenant-less): state explicitly that it validates migrations + allocation row only and never queries `backlog_items`, or the "never query without a tenant" invariant is unclear for that path.
Alert rule `increase(...[5m]) > 0` fires on any single transient 503; consider a threshold/duration to avoid paging on one-off admin probes.
SUMMARY: Solid fail-closed design: auth-first precedence, tenant-gated RLS scoping, explicit 503 mapping, and Go-only shipped logic all hold. Top risks are observability of the fail-closed startup path (metric unreachable when it matters), the TRUNCATE gap in the counter invariant, and startup/DB availability coupling; address before Gate 1.5.

NIT: ac_evidence entries all carry SHA "candidate" placeholders.
API contract adds a `storage` field not present in any AC — contract/AC drift.
Proof plan says red evidence is "404/no route"; 404-vs-401 semantics for an unauthenticated unknown path are not pinned.
MAJOR: Observability says "No new metrics required"; a fail-closed readiness endpoint with no log/metric for 503/latency leaves the primary failure mode undiagnosable (checklist item 10).
Admin-token verification is underspecified: constant-time comparison, token source/rotation, and whether PF_ADMIN_TOKEN falls foul of CL-005 (no PF token for internal callers) are not addressed.
Checklist item 2 unanswered: no on-startup DB check or alert lead-time for "PostgreSQL unavailable" beyond the request path.
Checklist item 1: "verified backup/restore path" not stated (read-only today, but must be declared explicitly as not-applicable rather than omitted).
Full-table `count(backlog_items)` scalability and index support are asserted ("single indexed read") but not evidenced; counts grow unbounded with backlog volume.
MINOR: out_of_scope is "Not specified" while AC-5 depends on it; must state "no PF-GP defs, no backlog item files, no new ID authority".
Rollback wording inconsistent: top-level "Revert the change" vs design_pack "Revert the edpsvc route"; no migration-interrupted recovery statement (checklist 6).
Checklist item 9 partial: redaction/retention of aggregate counts for the admin response is not stated; tenant leakage risk is only implicitly bounded by admin-only access.
CL-003: glossary terms (EDP admin token, authority, reserved_up_to, reservation) are not pinned to docs/GLOSSARY.md.
CL-001: ownership of `backlogAuthority` and of the `/backlog/*` route namespace (single writer, register point) is not declared.
BLOCKER: Design leaves affected_components, affected_files, and risks as "Not specified", so blast radius, the AC-5 diff-guard scope, and rollback ("Revert the change") are not objectively verifiable at Gate 1.
No statement that the runtime DB role used by edpdata.BacklogStore is least-privilege and NOT BYPASSRLS/superuser; checklist item 3 (privilege boundary) is unanswered for the new read path.
Behavior when migrations 0016/0017 are absent/unapplied is undefined — must be fail-closed 503, not 500 or a 200 with zeroed counts.
SUMMARY: Sound, low-risk, read-only pilot reusing existing mux and BacklogStore with clear fail-closed invariants and a red/green E2E proof plan.
Top risks: incomplete Gate-1 metadata (files/risks/out_of_scope), unspecified DB-role privilege/RLS posture, undefined behavior without migrations, and zero observability on the failure path.
Recommend Gate 1.5 only after the blocker items and checklist items 2/3/9/10 are explicitly answered in the design.

NIT: Verify `edp_backlog_authority_*` metric names/labels against the existing metric registry naming and label conventions before wiring.
0018 backfill over `backlog_id_reservations` may hold locks on large tables; consider lock_timeout/CONCURRENTLY-style mitigation and record expected migration duration.
MAJOR: Fail-closed gap: contract covers missing table/migrations but not the case where `backlog_id_allocations` exists yet the `authority='global'` row is absent — a zero-value row would yield a misleading 200; no-row must map to 503 (same as migration absent).

Counter drift acknowledged only for tests: no production reconciliation/detection path for `reservation_count` vs actual reservations (out-of-band deletes, partial writes) — drift silently corrupts the reported authority number with no alarm.

Alert lead-time missing: `edp_backlog_authority_startup_ok=0` and `edp_backlog_authority_errors_total` are emitted but no alert/on-call routing is defined, so defence-in-depth (checklist 2) stops at a log line.
MINOR: Status precedence for non-GET without a bearer (401 vs 405) is unspecified; pin the ordering in contract and tests to avoid handler-order drift.

"Scope guard rejects any new modified path outside the three implementation files" conflicts with the 8-file affected_files list (migrations, tests) — clarify the allowlist or the guard will fail legitimate migration/test edits.

`/ready` intentionally unchanged, so the service reports ready while backlog authority is broken; document this decoupling explicitly (and that it avoids restart storms) so future reviewers don't "fix" it inconsistently.
`item_count` is an unindexed full tenant `count(*)` under a 5s timeout; acceptable for admin-only use, but state the expected tenant cardinality bound or index dependency.
SUMMARY: Solid fail-closed, tenant-scoped, RLS-respecting design that follows the language rule and reuses existing owners; no blockers.
Top risks: zeroed-200 on a missing allocation row, undetected counter drift with no reconciliation, and metrics without an alert path.
Guardrails 2 (alerting), 6 (row-absent fail-closed case), and 10 (metric conventions) need explicit closure before Gate 1.5.

NIT: The fixed 503 message does not distinguish "migration missing" vs "row missing" for operators; consider a redacted, non-sensitive detail code in logs only (already partially covered by "redacted cause").
`reservation_scope`/`item_scope` labels are constant strings; harmless but could be inferred from the contract doc.
Duplicate declaration of scope/AC lists across `design_pack.scope`, `requirements`, and `acceptance_criteria` risks divergence at Gate 1.5 (CL-006 evidence hygiene).
MAJOR: Alert rule `increase(edp_backlog_authority_errors_total[5m]) > 0` fires on a single transient 503 (e.g., one timeout during a DB failover), guaranteeing alert fatigue and eroding trust in the runbook; needs a sustained-error threshold or burn-rate style condition.

Startup fail-closed is one-shot: no periodic re-check after boot, so if authority is lost at runtime the process stays "ready" and only endpoint errors reveal it; defence-in-depth (checklist #2) needs a continuous/readiness re-probe.

`to_regclass` table-presence check and the subsequent query are non-atomic (separate statements/transactions possible); a dropped/renamed table between check and read yields an unmapped error path — must be provably mapped to the fixed 503 message, not a generic 500.

Startup authority check appears to duplicate the handler's query/orchestration logic rather than calling the same `BacklogStore.Authority` path with a test proving parity; drift would let startup pass while the endpoint 503s (or vice versa).
MINOR: Counter trigger covers INSERT/DELETE on `backlog_id_reservations` but not UPDATEs or TRUNCATE; if any path reassigns rows or truncates, `reservation_count` silently drifts with no reconciliation query.

No explicit migration-interrupted recovery test (lock_timeout abort mid-up) — rollback statement covers the down path but checklist #6 asks for interrupted-apply recovery (idempotent re-run of 0018 backfill).

`item_count` full count per request under RLS is unbounded table growth over time; tenant+status index mitigates filter but not COUNT cost — consider cached/thresholded counting or documenting cost budget.
Success path emits no dedicated authority gauge/timestamp (only error counter + startup flag); detecting "stale but succeeding" authority requires log scraping.
BLOCKER: AC-5 requires running the scope guard against `engineering/trails/BI-PF-1508-scope-baseline.txt`, but that baseline file is absent from `affected_files`; creating it either violates the guard or leaves the test unfailable (no baseline → guard passes trivially).
No CI/workflow wiring for the scope guard is declared in `affected_files`, yet AC-5 asserts the guard runs and rejects out-of-scope paths; without a wired job this is untestable in the pipeline.
SUMMARY: Design is largely aligned: auth-first precedence, fail-closed 503, forced-RLS tenant scoping, Go language rule, and DB-trigger counter are sound and well-guarded.
Top risks: AC-5 scope guard is not wired with an in-scope baseline/CI hook (blocker), and alert/startup-check design lacks sustained-error thresholds and runtime re-probing (major).
Recommend resolving the baseline/CI declaration and alert tuning before Gate 1.5 approval.

NIT: Response field `storage: 'postgres'` is redundant with the contract but harmless; consider whether it should be a constant documented in the glossary (CL-003).
AC-2 pins tenant literal `product_forge` in tests — parameterize to avoid coupling tests to one tenant seed.
MAJOR: Ownership/route registration (CL-001) not explicitly answered: design must state who owns `/admin/*` routing in edpsvc and confirm no other owner already registers `/admin/backlog/*`; add an ownership assertion test if a registry exists.

`reservation_count` contract is inconsistent: AC implies reservation count may be tenant-relevant, but design queries `count(*) FROM backlog_id_reservations` globally with no RLS — a global count exposed alongside a tenant-scoped item count risks cross-tenant leakage; label both scopes explicitly in the response (e.g., `reservation_scope: global`).

Missing-migration detection is inferred solely from query error mapping to 503; no explicit check for migrations 0016/0017 (e.g., via schema version table) — a query error vs. missing-table is indistinguishable, weakening the observability claim in `/ready`.

Guard test for AC-5 uses a `git diff --name-only` allowlist that also whitelists the three implementation files implicitly inverted — verify the command as written actually fails on any *other* modified file (the exclusion patterns exclude the three expected files, so it detects stray changes; confirm direction and that it runs in CI, not just manually).
MINOR: `backlog_id_reservations` has no RLS; global count could grow unbounded and slow under load — add an index/existence note or accept documented timeout→503.

Reuse claim: `Authority` added to `BacklogStore` but response envelope construction may duplicate the existing admin error/envelope helpers — state explicitly that it reuses `authorized()`, `s.fail`, and the standard envelope.
405 for non-GET must be verified by a test; failure_matrix lists it but test_matrix has no corresponding test.

CL-005 (no PF token for internal callers) — confirm this endpoint is only for external/admin humans, not internal service-to-service calls; if internal callers exist, PF_ADMIN_TOKEN usage violates CL-005.

Checklist 2: no stated alert lead-time or startup check (defence-in-depth) for the readiness signal; `/ready` staying DB-connectivity-only means migration drift is only visible when this endpoint 503s.
SUMMARY: Design is sound and fail-closed: Go-only, RLS-scoped, no fallback, reversible with no schema change. Top risks: global vs. tenant scope labeling of `reservation_count`, explicit ownership of `/admin` routes, and making migration-absence detection and the AC-5 guard test explicit and CI-enforced.

BLOCKER: Prior AC-5 CI-wiring finding's disposition is wrong: `.github/workflows/pf-sb-scope-guard.yml` (or equivalent) is still absent from `affected_files`, so either the guard job does not exist or adding it violates the scope guard itself; AC-5 "guard runs in pipeline" remains unverifiable.
MAJOR: CL-010 not satisfied: `ac_evidence[].sha` is empty for all five ACs and `proof_plan.red_evidence` is prose ("returns 404 before wiring"), not attached current-run red proof; Gate 1.5 cannot verify the failing-before/passing-after claim from the design pack.
`design_pack.review.at` is empty and `reviewed_by: 'worker'` — review provenance is unattributed, so the impact_review verdicts are not auditable against the operating standard.
MINOR: Startup parity test pins tenant `'product_forge'` while the endpoint accepts arbitrary tenants; parity proof covers only one tenant binding path.
Actioned alert/metric changes (success timestamp, item_count gauge, reason codes) are evidenced only by runbook prose — no test or rule snippet in `affected_files` is referenced as executable proof.
NIT: `edp_backlog_authority_startup_ok` is now updated by the 5m recheck but retains a startup-only name; misleading when querying staleness.
Duplicate AC/scope lists across `acceptance_criteria`, `design_pack.requirements`, and `design_pack.scope` persist despite the prior disposition claiming a single source.
SUMMARY: Design is fundamentally sound and fail-closed, with most prior findings genuinely actioned (transaction-atomic reads, trigger coverage incl. TRUNCATE, alert hysteresis, parity test).
Top risks: CI wiring for the scope guard still undeclared in `affected_files` (AC-5 unmet), and CL-010 red-proof/SHA evidence remains prose-only, blocking Gate 1.5 verification.
Recommend resolving the workflow-file scope contradiction and attaching concrete red-run evidence before proceeding.

BLOCKER: ac_evidence for AC-5 cites `go/edpsvc/main_test.go`, but coverage/traceability/FR-5 cite `test-framework/tests/test_pf_sb_scope_guard.py`; AC-5 (scope guard) has no attached matching evidence, so CL-010/AC-5 is unverifiable from the delta pack.
All five `ac_evidence` entries share one identical sha `7e1afe78`, including the AC-5 entry whose file is wrong; a single blanket sha cannot substantiate per-AC current-run proof.
MAJOR: The delta `design_pack` omits keys that `spec_pack.applicability` still references: `contracts` (api/db/config), `runtime_contract`, `test_matrix`, `performance`, `security`, `rollout`, `rollback`, `observability` — dangling section references break spec-pack/Gate verification if this object is the authoritative value.
Delta `design_pack` also drops `version` (was 4) and the `invariants`/`guardrails`/`failure_matrix` rows; if the delta replaces the pack, invariant and rollback traceability for AC-4/AC-5 is lost.
`design_pack.controls` CTL check is `go test ./...` only, while AC-5's verification is the Python scope-guard test; the control row does not exercise the guard it claims to fail on.
MINOR: `design_pack.review_scope.files`/`components` were not updated in the same delta as `affected_files` (still omits `.github/workflows/pf-sb-scope-guard.yml`, `engineering/trails/…`, `engineering/evidence/…`), violating the "matching rows update in same delta" rule.
`coverage` rows show `runtime_capability: true` only for AC-1 and `false` for AC-2–AC-5 — inconsistent capability claim for endpoints covered by the same route handler.
`functional_spec` and `spec_pack` are listed as changed fields but retain `version: 1` and `functional_sha: 9599611f9678`; no re-hash accompanies the change.
NIT: Evidence artifacts (`red-proof.txt`, `scope-baseline.txt`) are placed inside `affected_files`, blurring CL-016's separation of prerequisites/evidence from code-change scope; consider a distinct evidence list.

Prior dispositions (workflow file, non-empty shas, review provenance) are now reflected in the delta; no reopen — but the AC-5 evidence row shows the fix was applied incorrectly rather than fully verified.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly wires the scope-guard workflow and red-proof into `affected_files` and fills review provenance, addressing the prior BLOCKER/MAJORs in intent.

Top risks: AC-5 evidence misattribution plus a blanket identical sha undermine the CL-010 fail-before/pass-after proof, and the reduced `design_pack` leaves multiple `spec_pack` section references dangling.
Resolve evidence/section integrity before Gate 1.5; remaining items are row-consistency hardening.

acceptance_criteria: GET /admin/backlog/authority?tenant=<tenant> without a bearer returns 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; status precedence is auth-first, so POST without a bearer is 401 and POST with a bearer is 405.

With a valid PF_ADMIN_TOKEN and tenant, GET /admin/backlog/authority returns 200 with authority=global, next_id from backlog_id_allocations, reservation_scope=global, reservation_count from the DB-maintained counter, tenant, item_scope=tenant, and item_count scoped to that tenant via forced RLS.
A missing tenant query parameter returns 400 and the handler never queries backlog_items without a tenant.
Missing migration 0016/0018, a missing global allocation row, DB outage, or query timeout returns 503 with a fixed backlog-authority-unavailable message; never a zeroed 200 or local/Git fallback.

An E2E test through edpsvc's real mux fails before the route is added and passes after it is wired; the scope guard rejects any new modified path outside the declared affected_files; no PF-GP agent/pipeline or backlog data files are changed.

requirements.title: Auth-first authority endpoint
outputs: 401 without token; 405 for POST with token
acceptance: Given no bearer When any method is called Then 401.
Given a bearer and POST When called Then 405.

requirements.title: Return authoritative counts
acceptance: Given valid token and tenant When GET Then 200 with authority fields.
Given missing allocation row When GET Then 503.

requirements.title: Tenant is mandatory
acceptance: Given no tenant When GET Then 400 and no item query.

requirements.title: Fail closed on authority loss
acceptance: Given missing migration/row or DB outage When authority is read Then 503 fixed message.

requirements.title: Counter and scope proof
outputs: counter parity and no out-of-scope paths
acceptance: Given reservation mutations When counter is read Then it matches.
Given a modified path outside affected_files When guard runs Then it fails.

nfr: Authority endpoint p95 within control-plane SLO
data_lifecycle: 0018 adds/backfills reservation counter; down drops counter artifacts only
rollback: Remove route/rule; migration 0018 down drops counter artifacts
